Photo By - Reuters Connect. CJ Bailey (11) leads NC State against Davis Warren (8) and Stanford. In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites tonight, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . NC State -6.5 NC State first half -3.5 NC State vs Stanford prop: NC State team total Over 31.5 After a shaky start to the year, CJ Bailey has been far more impressive in his last few starts. He's put up a 72+ QBR in four of the Wolfpack's last five games and should continue to play well enough for NC State to hit its team total Over at 32.5 or better . In his last three outings, he's finished with an adjusted completion percentage of 77.1% or higher while accounting for just two turnover-worthy plays. His efficiency has helped the Wolfpack climb to 37th nationally in pass success rate (47.6%) , which doesn't bode well for Stanford. The Cardinal allow the eighth-most passing yards per game in the Power Four (255.4) and are the only P4 program with fewer than five sacks and fewer than five interceptions. By Eric Rosales in College Football Published: October 23, 2026 at 7:37 pm EDT NC State brings a distinct offensive efficiency advantage into this Friday night clash Early NC State vs Stanford odds favor the visitors, but pacing will shape the game script Read below for our full NC State vs Stanford prediction Week 8 of the college football season brings a Friday night finale to the West Coast, where the Stanford Cardinal host the NC State Wolfpack. Kickoff is scheduled for 10:30pm ET on October 23. NC State enters as a sturdy road favorite at 3-3 and is desperate to snap a recent losing skid. Stanford sits at 3-4 and hopes to build on a recent victory by defending its home turf as a live underdog. Below, I break down my NC State vs Stanford prediction, spread and total picks, and the current Friday CFB odds. NC State vs Stanford Prediction Prediction: NC State wins by more than a touchdown in a game that stays under 55.5. For our NC State vs Stanford prediction, the offensive disparity is impossible to ignore. NC State fields a balanced offense, averaging 33.0 points per game while racking up 426.3 total yards per contest. The true mismatch emerges in crucial game-management situations. NC State is converting third downs at an elite 51.1% clip (45-for-88), exhausting opposing defenses and winning the field position battle. In stark contrast, Stanford's offense struggles to sustain drives, moving the chains on just 33.3% of its third-down attempts (32-for-96). Quarterback CJ Bailey provides excellent pocket presence for NC State, moving the chains consistently while capitalizing in scoring territory. NC State boasts an 85.2% red zone efficiency rate (23-for-27), ensuring its extended drives result in points. On the other side, Stanford will need a heavy dose of running back Micah Ford to shorten the game and keep Bailey on the sideline. NC State vs Stanford Picks Our NC State vs Stanford picks target the road favorite and the total. NC State vs Stanford Pick #1: NC State -7 Pick: NC State -7 (-108 at BetMGM ) We are laying the chalk with the road favorite. NC State's ability to convert on third downs gives it a massive structural advantage. With CJ Bailey successfully dissecting defensive coverages, NC State has the requisite firepower to win by more than a touchdown. BetMGM lists this line at a flat -7 with manageable juice, offering solid value for bettors who trust the superior offense. BetMGM promo code offers are available before kickoff to back the Wolfpack. NC State vs Stanford Pick #2: Under 55.5 Pick: Under 55.5 (-111 at BetMGM ) For my NC State vs Stanford total pick, I am backing Under 55.5. Stanford's clearest path to keeping this game competitive relies on grinding out the clock. By establishing the run and limiting total possessions, Stanford must drag the game's pace to a crawl. While NC State's red zone execution is stellar, Stanford's inability to hold up its end of the scoring bargain makes eclipsing 55.5 total points a tall order. We expect a physical, clock-draining game script that keeps the final score below the number. NC State vs Stanford Odds Alternate Spread NC State -6.5 Odds as of October 22, 2026, from BetMGM . away.headline: NC State loses 2 players for the season, several are questionable. Who's injured?
away.blurb: Head coach Dave Doeren said Monday that offensive lineman Yousef Mugharbil and tight end Vander Ploog are out for the season. Mugharbil sustained a lower leg injury during the Wolfpack’s 31-28 win over Louisville. He recorded a 64.4 offensive grade, according to Pro Football Focus, which was third on the offensive line. Mugharbil also graded out at 70 in pass blocking. The former transfer walk-on put together his best season of college football, earning a career-high 339 snaps. Ploog, a sophomore transfer from Oregon, played eight snaps against Virginia and one against Richmond. He came to Raleigh with a nagging shoulder injury, Doeren said, and could not get healthy. He will be able to return, but it won’t be until after the conclusion of this season. Ploog was spotted prior to the bye week leaving practice in a sling. Sowells was ruled out prior to the Wake Forest game. Doeren said Sowells will have a repair done and return to activities after his rehab is complete. He reiterated that the team hoped the center would be available this season, but the medical staff did not feel like it would make enough progress in the time frame remaining. Richardson was ruled out after the season opener. He sustained a season-ending bicep injury against Virginia and underwent surgery. N.C. State retakes the field this week following its second bye, but the roster continues to take hits. “Feel terrible for him,” Doeren said on Monday. “He was playing so good, and has been such a great leader on our offensive line, and has been through a lot. For those of you that know his story, it’s pretty significant what he went through at Florida. Good news is he has a year to recover fully and have a great season next year. But, in the moment, it hurts to lose such a good player on the offensive line.” Mugharbil collided with a semi-truck during his freshman year at Florida, days before the Gators’ season opener, ending his rookie season. He did not see game action during his time in Gainesville. Mugharbil transferred to Colorado but left shortly after arriving in Boulder. He returned to North Carolina and walked on with the Wolfpack before earning a scholarship and starting job. away.headline: NC State vs. Stanford injury report: Duke Scott among many players out
away.blurb: Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

away.headline: Stanford Injury Report Ahead of Season-Defining Matchup With NC State
away.blurb: But the program needs to get by without some key players. Ahead of the matchup, the ACC released official injury reports for this week. Stanford has multiple players still listed out, including linebacker Matt Rose and defensive back Brandon Nicholson. He has played at an elite level when healthy, but it is still to be disclosed how long he will be out. Stanford needs him back desperately to improve linebacker depth and production. Rose is the leader of the defense, and his presence elevates everyone around him. He's set to miss a significant amount of time, and it is highly possible that he will not return this season, putting the program in a tough spot. After Collin Wright missed time with an injury of his own last season, Nicholson shined and proved himself as a key player for the defense. Defensive backs Lonnie McAllister III and Chris Garland are questionable, while Lasiah Jackson is probable. NC State will be down some key stars as well. Running back Jayden Scott, defensive back Tristan Teasdell and tight end Vander Ploog headline the list of injured NC State players. Scott, NC State's leading rusher, has 62 carries for 358 yards and four touchdowns this season. With him out, it will be interesting to see how the Wolfpack's offense attacks. Wide receiver Jojo Trader and offensive tackle Kamen Smith are listed as questionable for the Wolfpack. If they return, they will provide a big boost. This game is big for both teams. For Stanford, a win puts them back at .500 and digs them out of a massive hole when it comes to returning to a bowl game. They would reach four wins, which is their total from last season, and would have a path to reaching a bowl game. That path evaporates with a loss. The Miami, Florida, native was rumored to be a top target for several schools looking for quarterbacks in his home state, but will return to an NC State team that will now have far higher aspirations following an 8-5 campaign that ended with wins in four of its past five games. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era in Ann Arbor will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. picks.headline: Predicting Final Score of Michigan Football vs. Indiana With Tommy Carr Under Center
picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Michigan Football vs. Indiana With Tommy Carr Under Center Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Very little has come easy for Michigan this season. The Wolverines needed a second Hail Mary attempt to beat Western Michigan, a final stop to take down Oklahoma, and a final stop to beat Penn State . Add in a game-winning touchdown pass by Iowa and Michigan has been on both sides of winning and losing on a play. And things likely don't get any easier whatsoever this weekend. Not only will Michigan host Indiana , the reigning national champions, but the Hoosiers come into Ann Arbor hungry . Indiana suffered its first loss since the 2024 season last weekend after Ohio State won by inches. LeBron's biggest comeback Story by Roundtable Sports Score Prediction: Hoosiers Look to Bounce Back Against Wolverines (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Brandon Brown Fri, October 23, 2026 at 9:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Indiana's perfect season came to an end last weekend, but the Hoosiers have absolutely nothing to be ashamed of following their 19-15 loss to Ohio State. Curt Cignetti's squad went toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the country and was just one properly executed play away from potentially leaving the field with a victory. Now comes another test. "Out of the frying pan and into the fire," Cignetti said on Monday in reference to facing Ohio State and Michigan in back-to-back weeks. How will Indiana respond to adversity for the first time this season? The Hoosiers are 6-1 and remain firmly in the conversation as one of the Big Ten's best teams. Saturday's matchup against Michigan provides an opportunity to prove that the loss to Ohio State was nothing more than a temporary setback. The Wolverines are coming off a win over Penn State, but they're also dealing with significant uncertainty at quarterback and have struggled to establish an offensive identity. Indiana should have several advantages in this matchup, particularly on defense. Indiana's offense vs. Michigan's defense Josh Hoover has been one of the biggest reasons for Indiana's success this season, and his ability to protect the football has been especially impressive. He has 18 touchdown passes and no interceptions through seven games. That's impressive for anyone, but it's especially noteworthy for Hoover since he arrived in Bloomington with a reputation as a turnover machine while at TCU. Even against Ohio State, Hoover put his team in position to win. His fourth-down throw to Nick Marsh in the end zone could have been and should have been the defining moment of Indiana's season, but Marsh stepped out of bounds and the Hoosiers came up just short. The important takeaway is that Hoover was capable of making that play against an elite opponent. Michigan presents another difficult challenge, particularly with its experienced secondary and the defensive approach of coordinator Jay Hill. The Wolverines have enough talent on the back end to make throwing the football difficult, so Indiana will need to be patient and avoid forcing unnecessary opportunities. Charlie Becker remains the biggest threat in the passing game, but Marsh is just as dangerous a weapon Michigan must respect. If Hoover can spread the football around and avoid turnovers, Indiana should eventually find opportunities for explosive plays. The running game will also be critical. Lee Beebe Jr. has already demonstrated his ability to carry the offense when needed, including his 203-yard performance against Northwestern. Turbo Richard is actually the lead dog in Indiana's backfield, so they have a one-two punch that rivals anyone in the nation. Establishing that rushing threat should make Hoover's job considerably easier. Indiana's defense vs. Michigan's offense This is where the Hoosiers have their clearest advantage. Michigan's offense has struggled for much of the season, and those issues ultimately resulted in Bryce Underwood being benched against Penn State. True freshman Tommy Carr took over in the second half, provided an immediate spark and helped the Wolverines escape with a 21-18 victory. Now Carr is expected to make his first career start against an Indiana defense that ranks among the nation's best. That's not exactly an ideal situation for Michigan. The Hoosiers rank fourth nationally against the run, which should create significant problems for a Wolverines rushing attack that ranks just 85th. If Indiana can contain Jordan Marshall, Savion Hiter and Carr on the ground, Michigan will be forced to rely heavily on its inexperienced quarterback. That's precisely the scenario Cignetti and his defensive staff should want. Indiana's defensive front has been outstanding, routinely creating problems for opposing offensive lines. Rolijah Hardy and Isaiah Jones are incredibly smart and opportunistic and are both solid tacklers. They provide additional toughness and athleticism at linebacker. The Hoosiers don't necessarily need to force Carr into mistakes immediately. Simply making Michigan play behind the chains and consistently face third-and-long situations should eventually produce opportunities for sacks and turnovers. Indiana has the defensive personnel to dictate how this game is played. Final thoughts and score prediction The loss to Ohio State was disappointing, but Indiana showed it belongs on the same field as the nation's elite programs. That performance should give the Hoosiers confidence rather than create doubt. Michigan is talented enough defensively to keep this from becoming a blowout, and Carr's mobility adds an element of unpredictability to the Wolverines' offense. Still, Indiana is the more complete football team. The Hoosiers should control the line of scrimmage defensively, limit Michigan's rushing production and gradually wear down the Wolverines with their offensive balance. Expect Michigan to hang around early before Indiana takes control in the second half, giving Cignetti's team an important bounce-back victory. Indiana 27, Michigan 17

LeBron's biggest comeback (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Brandon Brown Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:49 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Michigan picked up a much-needed 21-18 win over Penn State last weekend, but the Wolverines aren't exactly entering Saturday's matchup with Indiana firing on all cylinders. Kyle Whittingham's team needed a quarterback change at halftime to get things going offensively, and now true freshman Tommy Carr is very likely preparing for his first career start against one of the best defenses in college football. That's a pretty difficult assignment for a young quarterback, especially considering how Michigan has performed offensively throughout the season. Still, the Wolverines have some talented pieces on both sides of the ball, and they'll need just about everyone playing at their best to get a victory at home. Michigan's offense vs. Indiana's defense This is where things could get ugly for Michigan. Indiana enters the matchup ranked No. 4 nationally against the run, while Michigan is sitting at No. 85 in rushing offense. That's a massive mismatch on paper, especially when considering how much the Wolverines need their ground game to function in order to have any sort of offensive balance. Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter have both shown flashes, but neither has consistently provided the production Michigan needs. Throw Carr into the equation as a running threat, and the Wolverines at least have another dimension to work with. Whether that's enough against Indiana's outstanding defensive front remains to be seen. Guys like Mario Landino and Tyrique Tucker on the interior, and Tobi Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley off the edge, are going to make life difficult up front. Linebackers Rolijah Hardy and Isaiah Jones lead the Hoosiers in tackles and are very solid in the middle. If Michigan can't run the football, the responsibility falls almost entirely on Carr's shoulders. Indiana is No. 47 nationally against the pass, which is technically its weakest defensive area. That could create some opportunities for Andrew Marsh and JJ Buchanan, but asking a true freshman to consistently beat this defense through the air is a tall order, no matter how good his receivers are. Carr provided a spark against Penn State. Now we'll find out whether he can sustain that success against a significantly tougher opponent. Michigan's defense vs. Indiana's offense The Wolverines have a much better chance of competing on this side of the football. Jay Hill's defense has enough talent and experience to make Indiana uncomfortable, particularly in the secondary. Michigan has veteran defensive backs capable of challenging receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, although keeping those two contained for four quarters won't be easy. Both Becker and Marsh are two of the most dangerous receivers in the Big Ten, and Josh Hoover has done an excellent job taking care of the football — 18 touchdowns vs. zero interceptions says so. The Indiana quarterback has been impressive during this seven-game interception-free stretch, and Michigan desperately needs to find a way to end that streak. Generating pressure without sacrificing coverage will be important. Hoover has enough weapons to punish Michigan if he's consistently given time to survey the field. The Wolverines also have to account for Lee Beebe Jr. and Turbo Richard in the running game. Indiana's offensive balance makes it difficult to focus on any single area. Michigan's defense should be capable of producing stops, but the bigger question is whether the offense can capitalize when those opportunities arrive. Final thoughts and score prediction Michigan certainly has a path to making this competitive. The Wolverines need to establish some semblance of a running game, protect Carr from obvious passing situations and create a couple of turnovers defensively. Unfortunately, that's a lot to ask when it hasn't been the norm thus far, and against an Indiana team that has been consistently excellent throughout the season. I expect Michigan's defense to keep things relatively close through the first half, but Indiana's defensive front will eventually make life too difficult for Carr and the Wolverines. The Hoosiers have more offensive firepower, more consistency and the advantage of playing at home. Michigan 17, Indiana 27

Alright, let's pump the brakes a bit. Indiana wins by two touchdowns.

away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to replicate that effort against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. Where to watch LSU vs. Auburn live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Jordan-Hare Stadium -- Auburn, Alabama TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) LSU vs. Auburn prediction, picks What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable. Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double-digits. Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB The No. 20 LSU Tigers will hit the road to face the Auburn Tigers on Saturday. LSU is coming off a dominant win over Mississippi State, while Auburn upset Georgia last week. LSU has looked like two different teams at home and on the road. At Tiger Stadium, LSU is 5-0 with an average margin of victory of 36.2. On the road, the Tigers are 0-2 and have allowed 67 points. The LSU on SI staff made their picks for this week's big matchup. LSU defensive tackle Deuce Geralds celebrates. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Brooke Benedict Brooke Benedict I think LSU will be able to get a road win on its record against Auburn, as the team will come off major momentum from the Georgia upset next year and let details and mistakes slip that LSU will pick up on and be able to dominate in. LSU’s defense is also coming off serious momentum after shutting out No. 16-ranked Mississippi State last week, a defensive influence that will be a key factor in the game against the unranked Auburn Tigers. Auburn has the home-field advantage, which has been a major weakness for LSU so far this season. That’s what makes the stakes so much higher for LSU this weekend, an expectation that they will be able to meet. LSU 31, Auburn 20 LSU returns star TE Trey'Dez Green after weeks of an injury-induced absence, and the Tigers in purple and gold have their backs against the wall. As much as they control their own destiny, a third loss on the road would almost certainly eliminate them from playoff contention. Auburn is also coming off a huge win over Georgia on the road, and I don't believe that Goleshs' squad is ready for another physical battle like LSU will bring. I think LSU's defense, especially DJ Pickett and Ty Benefield, will disrupt Byrum Brown enough for Sam Leavitt and the offense to put their foot on the gas. LSU 34, Auburn 21 Zion Trammell It appears LSU's offense is getting a massive boost, as Trey'Dez Green is set to return after a multi-week absence. However, I think LSU will lean on Dilin Jones to control time of possession and grab an early lead. Defensively, LSU has to make Auburn a one-dimensional offense and keep Byrum Brown in the pocket. If they can accomplish that, I think LSU gets a big road win. LSU 31, Auburn 17 Louisiana State Tigers running back Dilin Jones. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JD Andress Auburn is coming off a massive win, and the Tigers continue to battle injuries, but the way Sam Leavitt has been playing lately makes it hard to pick against LSU. He's found a rhythm as a pure pocket passer, and for the first time this season, didn't throw an interception last week. He should continue to play at a high level, and when he does, LSU wins because of it. Adrian Martinez LSU will look to carry the momentum from its dominant shutout win over Mississippi State into a tough battle at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Even though Auburn is coming off the upset of Georgia, I expect the LSU to be up to challenge and the Tigers defense to be flying around the field, keeping Auburn in check. If LSU can protect the football and avoid the mistakes that have hurt them on the road this season, I think they come away with a much-needed SEC road victory. LSU 28, Auburn 13 LSU will prove that the struggles on the road shouldn't be a concern. The offense will start fast, like it's shown it can do consistently and the defense will be stifling from the jump. LSU will get out to that hot start, and only accelerate, extending the streak of scoring over 30 points. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Sam Leavitt of LSU and Byrum Brown of Auburn. Last week's upset makes the home dog easy to sell, but our LSU vs. Auburn predictions are built around the larger mismatch. The LSU Tigers bring the country's best opponent-adjusted net EPA profile to Jordan-Hare Stadium, while the Auburn Tigers still need Byrum Brown to manufacture too much of the offense himself. I'm laying the points with LSU and grabbing the Under as my best bet in this Tigers vs. Tigers affair. Head over to our latest college football picks for more Week 8 betting analysis. Who will win LSU vs Auburn: LSU -7.5 I would play the LSU Tigers to 50%. Last week's win over the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs absolutely raises the Auburn Tigers ' ceiling, but it took 26 Byrum Brown carries and three Gunner Stockton turnovers to pull it off. Additionally, Auburn is coming off one of its biggest wins in recent memory. I'm not here to tell you that LSU is a better football team than Georgia, but its profile may be more suitable for this matchup. The visitors sit No. 1 nationally in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play at +0.44 , while Auburn is 35th at +0.14. Brown is Auburn's engine on the ground, yet he ranks 100th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's a dangerous imbalance against a defense that can crowd the box and still trust its coverage. Jordan-Hare will have some real juice too, with belief injected into Auburn's season. However, LSU's down-to-down edge should create separation over 60 minutes. TOP PICK LSU vs Auburn Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The Under is my top pick in this matchup, and I'd play it to 49.5. Brown is producing 0.41 EPA per rush, fourth among qualified runners, and a heavy quarterback-run plan is the best way to keep the game close . That also bleeds clock. LSU's defense has held opponents to 4.35 yards per play and a 39.2% success rate, while Auburn's unit ranks 31st in adjusted EPA allowed and gives up 5.15 yards per snap . LSU's offense is good, but its opponent-adjusted efficiency ranks 25th rather than among the elite. Also, I still have not seen enough from Sam Leavitt to trust him to make game-defining plays. I don't think his head coach has either. LSU can control field position and reach the low 30s. Auburn landing in the teens leaves enough room for Under 51.5. LSU vs Auburn combo The prevailing theme throughout is LSU's defense. It controls the game, wins the game for the Tigers, and keeps it low-scoring throughout. That holds true early on, which is why I added the first-quarter Under to this combo beyond the previously mentioned two plays. I don't expect either team to come out guns blazing through the air due to decision-making concerns tied to the quarterback. That's particularly true early in the game when the emphasis on either to score quickly is minimal. That should keep the clock running most of the first quarter and start off this heavily correlated combo out strong. Lane Kiffin and No. 17 LSU football are about find out as they travel to Auburn for a renewal of an old SEC rivalry Saturday, Oct. 24 (11 a.m. CT, ABC). One of Kiffin's coaching mentors, former Alabama and LSU head coach Nick Saban , who obviously is quite familiar with Auburn, has said he believes Auburn's football stadium haunted. Weird or "magical," as Kiffin put it earlier this week, things happen inside the venue and Auburn has snatched wins from the jaws of defeat plenty of times over the years. All that is to say, LSU (5-2, 2-2 SEC) might need to contend with some juju Saturday at Auburn (4-2, 2-2). AUBURN IN A LETDOWN SPOT? Lane Kiffin says 'relief syndrome' could hinder Auburn vs LSU football IS JORDAN-HARE STADIUM? Bruce Pearl once told Lane Kiffin Jordan-Hare Stadium was haunted. What the LSU coach thinks Can LSU football QB Sam Leavitt keep a clean sheet? When junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has avoided turnovers, LSU has easily won this season. Last time out against Mississippi State, Leavitt took care of the football and worked efficiently and smart. It paid off with a 31-0 victory. Auburn has been opportunistic this season when teams have turned the ball over. Georgia fumbled late in the game last weekend, allowing Auburn to go down and kick a game-winning field goal as time expired to pull off the upset in Athens. Kiffin said earlier this week that he and his staff will highlight the importance of ball security. "As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make," Kiffin said. "It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home." LSU football offensive staff familiar with Auburn QB Byrum Brown When LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. was South Florida's offensive coordinator under then-head coach Jeff Scott, he helped open up the recruiting process to bring Brown to the Bulls . So Weiss is familiar with Brown's game as LSU gears up for this matchup. "Really hard player to tackle, similar to playing (South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers) that way. They're different styles, but they're really strong through a lot of arm tackles," Kiffin said of Brown. "He seems really smart by the way that he plays." Brown played for Auburn head coach Alex Golesh at South Florida before following him to The Plains out of the transfer portal. LSU offense should get plenty of opportunities It's hard to score if the offense doesn't have the ball or the ability to extend drives with it. Through six games, Auburn ranks 133rd in college football in time of possession. At 26:54, Auburn is dead-last in the SEC in time of possession. But the situation is not quite like that with Ole Miss , which is second-to-last in the league in time of possession because it operates and scores quickly. Auburn scores just 26.8 points per game, which comes in 13th out of 16 teams in the SEC. While Auburn does convert third downs 46% of the time, its offense only converts touchdowns in the red zone at a 65% clip. Defenses have racked up 23 sacks against Auburn and have caused 15 Auburn turnovers to this point. All of that adds up to LSU's offense likely winning the time of possession battle. The onus, then, will be on LSU to cap drives with points. Lane Kiffin vs first-year head coaches this season It's a small sample size, but Kiffin has not found success against teams with first-year head coaches this season. It also happens that the two matchups with coaches in their first year at their programs were LSU's two road games so far this season. Still, LSU lost both of those road games at Ole Miss against Pete Golding and at Kentucky against Will Stein. That same trend is presenting itself Kiffin again, this time it's Golesh at Auburn. Golesh was the coach at South Florida from 2023 to 2025 before taking the Auburn job over the offseason. While at USF, Golesh hosted Saban and Alabama in 2023 and pushed the Crimson Tide to the brink before falling 17-3. So, this game likely won't be easy for LSU. Kiffin will look to buck the trend against Golesh at Auburn this weekend. LSU football vs Auburn prediction If you are a believer in trap games or letdown spots, LSU's road game at Auburn is a hard game to handicap. One could argue this is a trap game for LSU — also factor that this game kicks of at 11 a.m. — while Auburn comes into the showdown off the program's biggest win in some time, knocking off No. 1 Georgia on the road. Only thing that feels certain about this game is that Jordan-Hare will be rocking and odd things take place in that building. Look for an ugly, sloppy, sleepy game. LSU squeaks one out in the end. As it stands, the Tigers are a seven-point underdog to their rival Tigers, though CBS Sports' Austin Nivison believes the Tigers will lose by at least 10 points . Here's why. "What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable," he wrote. "Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits." In fact, every CBS analyst polled about the game took Lane Kiffin's squad to win straight-up, but a few, like Chip Patterson and David Cobb, predicted the Tigers to at least cover the spread. It's certainly a difficult matchup for the Tigers, who could be experiencing what Kiffin called 'relief syndrome' after their win against Georgia. There is a path to the Tigers winning this game, though, and it seems to run through Byrum Brown. "If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense," Nivison continued. "That worked last week in Athens... The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs." Brown seemed to have been contained a bit in earlier games, as his number was called for design plays quite rarely, but against the Dawgs, Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon leaned on Brown's legs to get the Tigers' offense moving. It worked to great effect last week, but LSU will now be even more prepared for Brown's dual-threat nature, which adds a layer of complexity to the Tigers' playcalling this week. The Tigers, coming off a marquee win, are looking to continue their momentum, and having home-field advantage should play a big part in their matchup with Kiffin's Tigers. However, LSU has answers for most of Auburn's offensive production, so the Tigers will likely need to get creative if they want to emerge from the Tiger Bowl with a win. away.headline: Early SEC availability report for Auburn's SEC game vs. LSU revealed
away.blurb: The initial SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report is out for this week's matchup between the Auburn Tigers and the No. 17 LSU Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium, and Auburn will enter the game with a relatively clean bill of health. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring remain "out" for Auburn, which has been the case since SEC play began in Week 3. However, one addition has been made. Defensive lineman Saint Farrior is listed as "questionable" for Saturday's game against LSU, meaning it is uncertain as of Wednesday whether he will be available to play. LSU will be without linebacker Will Weeks, safety Dashawn Speans, wide receiver Phillip Wright, and linebacker Charles Ross on Saturday, while defensive tackle Richard Anderson is listed as "doubtful." Wright is the most notable name on the report with three catches for 70 yards and a touchdown in LSU's season-opening win at Clemson. He has not played since Week 2 against Louisiana Tech. Linebacker Whit Weeks will miss his fourth straight game after he suffered a leg fracture in LSU's win over Texas A&M last month. Despite several players being out, LSU got good news Wednesday as wide receiver Jackson Harris, tight end Trey'Dez Green, and defensive end Princewill Umanmielen were left off the initial availability report and are expected to play this Saturday at Auburn. Harris leads LSU wide receivers with 456 yards and five touchdowns, and Green has 222 receiving yards and a touchdown this season. Umanmielen, who followed head coach Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss, leads the team in sacks with eight and is fourth in tackles with 27. Farrior played three snaps in Auburn's win over Georgia last week and has played in just four games this season for 17 total snaps. According to the SEC's website, "SEC school personnel must submit availability reports three days before each football game, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to game time." Inaccurate reports could result in fines between $25,000 and $100,000. Auburn will face LSU on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT. Taylor Jones is the lead writer for Auburn Wire, part of the USA TODAY Network. away.headline: Injuries Are Mounting at a Concerning Rate For LSU
away.blurb: However, LSU hasn't left a game unscathed this year. Princewill Umanmielen and Jackson Harris exited the game with injuries and didn't return. "Yeah, both didn't return, which again not a lot of pity for injuries, all the ones coming in, the two number sevens don't play for us and haven't been playing, and then another significant player in him [Umanmielen] goes out early and wasn't able to return," Kiffin said. "The doctors held him, which obviously was the right thing to do, so that's all I got for you." Kiffin isn't wrong. Trey'Dez Green, Whit Weeks, and Dashawn Spears were already out for this game. If Umanmielen and Harris miss time, the Tigers' depth is thin. LSU deserves credit for hanging on without its key stars, but eventually, they won't have enough firepower to win. Injuries Are Mounting at a Concerning Rate For LSU Skip to main content SI.COM The LSU Tigers dominated the Mississippi State Bulldogs on Saturday, cruising to a 31-0 victory. The Tigers were against the wall, and Lane Kiffin's team responded with a big-time win. They join a long list of injured players on the roster. LSUTigers defensive end Princewill Umanmielen (1) looks on during the second quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Bulldogs were without starting quarterback Kamario Taylor, but Kiffin said his team is banged up as anyone. The Bulldogs were without starting quarterback Kamario Taylor, but Kiffin said his team is banged up as anyone. "I know you're going to talk about injuries, and that'll be a storyline, but hey, there ain't any team in America that has more significant players standing on the sideline than us," Kiffin said. "So not a lot of pity there." Umanmielen left in the first quarter, and Harris limped off the sideline in the third quarter. Jordan Ross stepped up in Umanmielen's absence, recording a sack and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kiffin didn't have a firm update on either player after the game. "We had a lot of people sitting on our sideline and won 31-0," Kiffin said. "This team was built to be a championship team with significant players and starters that I still say can match up with anybody if we were healthy. And when those injuries happen, it's hard." While some star players are recovering, LSU has to stay afloat. The Tigers will hit the road to face Auburn, which is coming off a big-time upset over Georgia. While it's an early kickoff, Joran-Hare Stadium will be rocking next week. After the Auburn game, LSU will get a much-needed bye week before a difficult stretch against Alabama, Texas, and Tennessee. Pete Fiutak Fri, October 23, 2026 at 6:10 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, South Carolina has become the proverbial Team You Don't Want To Face. It was only one game a few weeks ago in horrendous conditions, but the Gamecocks' 38-19 win over Florida showed one thing more than anything else – they're still trying. This was supposed to be a big bounceback season for South Carolina, but it lost three straight SEC games, including an overtime home game to Kentucky, and that was it. No SEC title, no CFP appearance. It was all over, and it wasn't even the second week of October. This is a good Gamecock team in the fun make-lemonade-out-of-the-season position of getting to screw everyone else up. Tennessee has to keep its focus and show that it's worthy of being in the mix for all the things South Carolina was supposed to be fighting for right now. It beat Alabama, it took out Auburn by ten, and it probably should've beaten Texas. Now it has to sidestep the landmine. Tennessee vs South Carolina: Quick Hits The Vols get a week off before hosting Kentucky, and then they're off to Texas A&M. South Carolina goes to Oklahoma next week before hosting Texas A&M. The two haven't played since Tennessee won 41-20 in 2023. The Vols are 4-1 in the last five meetings. The Tennessee running game was okay in the win over Alabama, and George MacIntyre kept his cool, throwing for close to 200 yards. But the offense turned it over twice and was hardly smooth. The Volunteer defense held Bama to 201 yards of total offense and forced four takeaways because of the ten tackles for loss and five sacks that dominated the game. Tennessee is No. 1 in the nation in sacks, and it's about to force the Gamecocks into a whole slew of mistakes. Why South Carolina Will Win How did South Carolina blow out Florida? LaNorris Sellers showed the upside to be a dangerous NFL quarterback. The offense didn't turn the ball over, and the defense pitched a gem, especially against the run. Tennessee has a good offense, but it's the defense that delivers the mail. South Carolina can't get frustrated. It needs to keep the mistakes to a bare minimum and be okay with living to fight another day. Tennessee vs South Carolina Prediction, Betting Lines It is possible to run on the Tennessee defense. It'll get its sacks and plays behind the line, but Auburn was able to run well against the Vols. It lost because it turned the ball over three times. Arch Manning was actually okay against the Vols, but the two Texas turnovers and 11 penalties made it way too close. The weather had a lot to do with the three Florida turnovers against South Carolina. It's going to be 72 and sunny on Saturday in Columbia. LeBron's biggest comeback Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Zach Ragan Tue, October 20, 2026 at 4:52 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers will travel to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. "Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?" said McElroy. "Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. "I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon." "Tennessee's defense is amazing," added McElroy. "They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks." Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. LeBron's biggest comeback SARAH PHIPPS/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK Zach Ragan Fri, October 23, 2026 at 5:51 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers will take on the South Carolina Gamecocks in Columbia this weekend. Former Oklahoma head coach Bob Stoops did not pick Tennessee to beat Alabama last weekend. This week, though, Stoops is going against the grain and picking Tennessee to beat South Carolina (nearly everyone in the national media has picked the Gamecocks to beat the Vols in Columbia on Saturday). "That surprised the heck out of me," said Stoops when it was noted that South Carolina is favored to beat Tennessee. "I saw that earlier in the week. But I'm going to take Tennessee. "I just think overall they're playing really well and South Carolina has shown some hiccups. … I'm going to take Tennessee. Their defense is really playing great. … I just really think the defense has made a difference for Tennessee." Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Tennessee-South Carolina predictions: Why are Gamecocks favored over Vols?
picks.blurb: Tennessee is coming off a massive win over Alabama . So naturally, South Carolina is favored over the Volunteers in Saturday's matchup in Columbia. The Gamecocks had a week to relish in their impressive road upset of Florida and rest up during their bye, while many are expecting a Vols letdown after such an emotional high and a field-storming last week. SEC letdowns have been popular this season: Ole Miss lost to Florida after beating LSU. Florida lost to Missouri after beating Ole Miss. Georgia lost to Auburn after beating Alabama . And there's a reason Tennessee fans are more worried than you think fans of the 11th-ranked team playing a 3-3 team should be. The Vols' last trip to Columbia in 2022 ended with a blowout loss that knocked them out of College Football Playoff contention. Tennessee vs South Carolina predictions, expert picks USA TODAY Sports staff picks : John Brice: Tennessee Matt Hayes: South Carolina Jordan Mendoza: South Carolina Paul Myerberg: Tennessee Erick Smith: South Carolina Eddie Timanus: South Carolina Blake Toppmeyer: Tennessee Austin Curtright: South Carolina 31, Tennessee 27 John Leuzzi: South Carolina 24, Tennessee 21 Jordan Mendoza: South Carolina 26, Tennessee 23 LaNorris Sellers was awesome in leading the Gamecocks to an upset of Florida two weeks ago. He threw four touchdown passes and averaged eight yards per attempt. George MacIntyre was … fine as the Volunteers took down Alabama, primarily with a dominant defensive effort. It’s hard not to lean toward Sellers, as it looks like he might be getting hot. South Carolina 27, Tennessee 17 — Adam Bittner, USA TODAY Sports This is a major trap game for Tennessee on the road after an emotional win, but its defense should travel just fine. The matchup may be decided by who's better between Vols running back DeSean Bishop and the Gamecocks' run defense that ranks third in the SEC. Oddsmakers slightly favor South Carolina in a spot that feels ripe for an unranked-over-ranked result. Still, picking against Tennessee's defense has been a fool's errand. Tennessee 24, South Carolina 21 . — Emmett Siegal, Knoxville News Sentinel Tennessee's win over Alabama is nothing to ignore but South Carolina also had a statement win right before an extra week to get healthy with the open date. The Vols keep it close but the home crowd and older quarterback prevail. South Carolina 24, Tennessee 17 . — Lulu Kesin, Greenville News Tennessee-South Carolina injury report After South Carolina was missing starting defensive back Quay'sheed Scott, defensive lineman Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy, edge rusher Julian Walker and starting center Carter Miller against Florida on Oct. 10, only Miller and Scott of the four are on the report this week. Scott is doubtful and Miller is listed as questionable. There were no new injured Tennessee players listed on the initial SEC student-athlete availability report for the game against South Carolina. However, seven Tennessee players have already suffered season-ending injuries: starting left guard Wendell Moe ; starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body). Is South Carolina favored vs Tennessee? Betting odds, spread (via BetMGM ) Favorite : South Carolina by 2 points Over/under : 50.5 total points Moneyline : South Carolina -130, Tennessee +110 Who will start at QB for Tennessee: George MacIntyre or Faizon Brandon? Josh Heupel refused to name a starter for Saturday's game, but the Vols will likely stick with George MacIntyre under center for a third straight game. MacIntyre is 2-0 as a starter and completed 21-of-31 passes for 197 yards and an interception in Tennessee's 26-10 win over Alabama last week. Faizon Brandon, who won the starting QB job out of camp, dressed but did not play vs. the Crimson Tide. "MacIntyre … you see him continuing to get better each and every week," Shane Beamer said . "With his ability to run the offense, get rid of the ball when it's not there in the passing game, sit in the pocket, throw the ball downfield, but make good decisions and continue to play winning football. And that's what I think both those guys are doing a great job of is playing winning football.” Is Dylan Stewart playing vs Tennessee? Is South Carolina star pass rusher back from suspension? Yes The Gamecocks edge rusher returned for the Florida game after serving a one-game suspension for multiple incidents in South Carolina's Sept. 26 loss to Alabama, which included punching a Crimson Tide player. Against Florida, Stewart had his best performance of the season, with five tackles (four solo), two forced fumbles, one sack and one tackle for loss. Pro Football Focus gave him a career-best 95.8 grade for his defense and a 92.7 pressure grade, the second-highest in his three seasons. "He was awesome throughout the game, his impact on the field is evident," Shane Beamer said. "He's a special talent in the way that he's able to affect other teams' offenses . . . I thought he did a great job, not just against the pass, but I really think thought he played the run well, just fitting gaps and being where he was supposed to be. "... "This will be a huge couple weeks for him and should see an even better version of him against Tennessee." What channel is Tennessee-South Carolina game on? After a two-game losing streak (against the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars) to start the Big 12 schedule, they bounced back with a big victory against Kansas. A win against the Sun Devils would give the Wildcats a two-game winning streak in the conference. It would also keep them in the race for the Big 12 title game and a berth in the College Football Playoff. All of the signs are pointing toward Johnson playing this weekend in Tempe. The Wildcats coaching staff is likely just being cautious about his status. So expect him in uniform for Saturday's game If not, things could get dicey for the Wildcats. None of the backups have any real experience. It will be even tougher considering they are playing on the road against a conference rival. The hope is Johnson is ready to go to help the Wildcats' chance of moving three games ahead of .500.

away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. More Videos The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

picks.headline: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET BASKETBALL NEWS Saturday night marks a crossroads for the Clemson Tigers and head coach Dabo Swinney, who welcome in the Virginia Tech Hokies in a highly-anticpated matchup. Memorial Stadium should be sold out this weekend, and Swinney will look to continue the strong stretch coming out of the open date. However, when looking at the advanced analytics, it could mean that Clemson has to survive a strong test from the Hokies to pick up its third ACC win of the season. Fortunately for fans, there tends to be a lean towards the Tigers in that department, according to Versus Sports Simulator . It gives Clemson a 64% chance to win on Saturday, with an average score being around 29-23. This contest has been one that has constantly switched in the projections, due to the losses that both teams have had since the month of October began. Virginia Tech had a two-game skid against Pitt and Cal, losing by a score in both games, to be forced to win out for the remainder of the season. However, when the month began, the Tigers only had a 53% chance to win. The model gives Swinney’s group a defense with a B+ grade, while the offense is generously given a B- grade. That’s how Clemson has won games over the course of this season, with the defense leaving enough points on the board for the Tigers to score on sporadic occasions. On the flip side, Virginia Tech is given a C+ overall ranking by Versus, with its best quality being a B- offense. However, it’s important to note that the Hokies’ defense, although graded a C+, leads the country in tackles for loss and is also first in the ACC in sacks and forced fumbles. Regardless, Clemson is expected to hit the ground running, with this amount being the most it has scored against a Power Four opponent at all this season. The home-field advantage plays a small factor in the Tigers' favor, with betting markets having them favored by about a field goal. Even with the game being at Memorial Stadium, Versus has Clemson as the favorite regardless of where the game is. If the game were at Lane Stadium, Swinney’s group would have a 52% chance to win the game on Saturday. However, there’s much more to a game than the model itself, but the advanced analytics show advantages on Clemson’s end that perhaps others aren’t thinking about. Swinney will look to reinforce that at home on Saturday, playing a team that will be playing with hopes to remain in the ACC Championship contention pool. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on ESPN.
