(Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images C_Craft Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:41 PM UTC · 11 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nitty Gritty Time Has Arrived for 2026 Greetings once again STS readers! Dabo Swinney always says each week is the "biggest game of the year" but even he has conceded that some games have more juice than others. This would have to be considered one of those games. While it isn't on the scale of a top-ten matchup, or even what it might have been back in 2011 when Clemson traveled to face VT or when they saw the Hokies again in the ACC title game, it is a vital tipping point for both teams looking to regain relevance. The winner of this game stays firmly in the hunt for a chance to go to Charlotte. Reaching 10 wins would be a huge accomplishment for this year's Tigers, and despite the two lopsided losses, it would be a step back up after 2025's major letdown. Before we get to the matchup, here is my good, bad, and ugly from last week's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern. The Good: Clemson's defense was lights out beyond a few moments during CSU's first drive when their scripted plays found some success ahead of a missed FG attempt. I was most encouraged by how well the depth performed, particularly in the secondary, as they got subbed more and more into the game. The upgrade in secondary execution across the board cannot be understated after last year's debacles. Clemson's special teams continues to shine week in and week out. I said Chris Johnson, Jr. was on the verge of scoring a kickoff return and nearly did it on his one opportunity. Nolan Hauser continues to look like an NFL starter and the coverage team produced a turnover for a touchdown for loyal Tiger Kylon Griffin. The Bad: Red zone offense wasn't ugly because the Tigers did punch in touchdown runs from CJJ and Gideon Davidson, but obviously there were more missed chances and bad penalties that continue to haunt this year's offense inside the 20 yard line. 37 points easily could have been 57 points or more considering the defensive and special teams dominance. The Ugly: Clemson's downfield passing attack gets the nod for the ugly. Especially when Tait Reynolds delivered plenty of throws that were there for big-money WRs TJ Moore and Bryant Wesco. Reynolds also apparently missed Moore running wide open on a post at least once, but lack of WR production and TDs were not on Chad Morris's play calls. He's getting 1 on 1 scenarios for the outside guys and they need to pay those off the way they are being paid to do. Clemson can't afford to miss those in these next stretch of games. Now that we are done with that, on to the 5-2 Hokies. Clemson Offense vs. VT Defense: There are several reasons to have some apprehension as a Clemson fan looking at this game. Clemson's running attack has proven to be much further along than the downfield passing game. It isn't a coincidence that Clemson has run the ball effectively in the 4 wins and failed miserably to do so in the 2 losses. Clemson's passing attack has yet to prove it can go win if it has to and VT's defense has been good against the run so far this season. They have given up a lot of passing yards, however, but can Reynolds and the offense deliver enough to exploit that apparent weakness? Any DC with a functional brain is going to try to force Reynolds to throw to win, which will mean loading up on the run and sending pressures regularly. Clemson fans are going to get another real sign if the OL has gotten its act together more with the new (and reportedly best) group of five guys out there together. VT is a pressure defense and looks to force the issue which has helped them rack up good sack and TFL numbers as well as effective run defense, but likewise has opened them up to getting burned on explosives (especially in the passing game). Clemson desperately needs to hit on the explosive play chances that are going to be there and, of course, limit VT's ability to get them behind the chains. Dabo has harped on the team not winning the turnover margin in games this season. Clemson is certainly due to do that, but it starts with the offense not turning it over. Clemson ended up throwing the ball 44 times in the Miami game, and that number needs to be between 25-30 this week I think if Clemson is going to win. This team is not equipped to play shootout football right now, and VT is much more capable of that and has had those types of games already. Reynolds has cut down on putting the ball in jeopardy, and a big part of that is having better pass protection to begin with, but he's been a little loose with the ball as a runner. Reynolds managed to avoid a bad turnover last week when he pounced on his own fumble, but the margin of error is not big in any of these remaining games to overcome putting the ball on the ground. I discussed the Moore/Wesco duo earlier, but it is imperative one or both deliver and win their matchups that VT is going to present them with in order to try to force Clemson away from the running game. I liked a lot of the concepts Morris showed to get the ball to the outside guys in various ways, including using bootlegs with Wesco coming across where you traditionally use a tight end. TJ Moore has been best on the slant in the RPO game, but he needs to win more of the outside fade situations that he has not been nearly as good with this season. Gordon Sellars is out with a concussion, and that eliminates at least one of the plan B options that Chad Morris very thinly veiled that he desired to have to push Moore when he has his press conference on Wednesday. Clemson needs the 2024 Texas game or 2025 SMU game version of TJ Moore on Saturday night. VT is similar in some ways to Miami defensively in that their front is stronger than their secondary. Clemson was unable to exploit Miami enough outside to offset being beaten at the point of attack that night. Clemson still needs to get at least 100 net yards rushing to keep that part of the offense relevant. The running back room is plenty good enough to deliver with Jay Haynes now back with Davidson and Johnson. They need to be given ample chances to deliver in this game. Clemson Defense vs. VT Offense : Clemson's defense is certainly ahead of the offense in the growth department. Part of this is because the big money guys on this side of the ball are playing like they are big money guys more consistently. This will be a real test considering VT has at least one playmaker at WR, RB, and TE to go with an NFL prospect at QB. Clemson has to make sure that VT can't get its running game going with Jeffrey Overton because he can hurt you badly if you let him get loose. BC found this out in nasty weather when Overton cooked them for 209 yards. Pittsburgh escaped with a win over the Hokies despite giving up nearly 500 yards of offense and 33 points, but one big reason was VT couldn't run the ball and passing more led to more turnovers. Ethan Grunkemeyer is a good player as Clemson fans saw last year when he handled the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl, but you still want him having to attack the strength of Clemson's back end versus having the balance of the running game to set things up and protect him. I worry the most about VT using Overton in the screen game and their dynamic tight end Luke Reynolds because those guys will match up with Clemson's nickel, safeties, or linebackers and not Ashton Hampton or Elliot Washington. It will be vital to make Grunkemeyer hold the ball so the rush can get there and get hands in the passing lanes on VT's RPO game. VT can be turned over, but that depends a lot on getting them into more obvious passing scenarios and heating Grunkemeyer up. Penn State was able to manage enough of a run game and largely keep Clemson's depleted defensive front from bothering him last year in the bowl game. He can really hurt you if you let him stand there and get through his reads. Clemson isn't going to keep VT under 100 yards and shut them out like they did CSU unless they deliver in some crazy way that far surpasses expectations. VT has too much talent to not have some success, but Clemson's ability to turn them over and force field goal attempts will be massive. Clemson can win a game in the 20s, but allowing VT to get to 30 or more probably means a big fat L for the Tigers on Saturday night. Getting VT at home helps for sure because they have been way better in Lane Stadium than on the road, such as when they allowed a depleted California squad to take them down. VT has been a fast-starting team, which usually means they are good at their opening 12-15 play script, so Clemson needs to be locked in right away on defense. Special Teams: Most fans who have been around since the 2000s know how much special teams helped Frank Beamer elevate VT to a top 20 program. It certainly was a major factor when Clemson lost a critical game with the Hokies back in 2007. Ironically, now the Tigers have the differential special teams play heading into this matchup thanks to outstanding work across the board under Rich Bisaccia. Returns look dangerous, coverage has been largely terrific, and Nolan Hauser has to be among the frontrunners for the Lou Groza Award. This game is pretty close on paper for sure, so this phase could be the difference. None of Clemson's games has featured a special teams fake this season, so Clemson has to be alert. Fortunately there hasn't really been any reason for Clemson to try to get fancy on returns or on kicks. The closest thing was Nolan Hauser's pooch punt at California that paid off with a roughing penalty, but that is exactly why you run something like that on a defense that isn't prepped to defend a punt. Overall: There is a lot about this 2026 team that reminds me of the 2021 team. I ended up really liking that 21 team mainly because they showed real toughness to overcome the obvious warts and squeezed 10 wins out of a team that easily could have only won 7. That isn't what you want year in and year out as a fan, especially when "Best is the Standard" is written in your facility, but this team has always been more about getting back to being tough. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.blurb: Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." home.headline: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out
home.blurb: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out Skip to main content About One talking point going into the game, and really a talking point each week, is injuries and how they are going to affect depth charts for both teams. On Wednesday, the initial injury report for the game was released, and Virginia Tech cornerback Cam Chadwick was listed as questionable. On Thursday, another name was dropped, and the UConn transfer was off the list, which is a good sign. However, a couple of names still popped up for the Hokies who sound like they'll be game-time decisions at best. Offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham and cornerback Thomas Williams were both listed as questionable. As far as Clemson goes, defensive tackle Vic Burley is listed as questionable. When Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech, you knew that attendance at games was not going to be an issue with the Hokies' fans. Heck, they came out in droves last season, with a dismal season that saw Brent Pry fired after a Week 3 loss at home to Old Dominion. There are still two more home games remaining on the slate for Franklin and his team this season, and it was announced that those two final games will be played in front of a full house. The game on Nov. 14 against Stanford was already sold out, but now Virginia Tech has officially sold out the Commonwealth Clash against Virginia on Nov. 28. To think, Virginia Tech didn't even need to have two-for-one promos to get it sold out in late November. This is expected to be one of the better Commonwealth Clashes in some time. Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball Coming off a 34-24 victory at home over Georgia Tech last Saturday, the Virginia Tech football team will hit the road for the first of two road games sandwiched around their bye week on Oct. 31 in Death Valley in South Carolina against Clemson. The Hokies will be looking to become bowl-eligible with a win after winning five of their first seven games, while the Tigers come in at 4-2 in a battle in primetime on ESPN between a pair of two-loss ACC teams in late October. NEW AVAILABILITY REPORT Cam Chadwick is off the report for the Hokies, while DT Vic Burley has been added for Clemson. pic.twitter.com/yEN9gsML54 Freshman Benjamin Eziuka played nearly 50 snaps against the Yellow Jackets last weekend and will be ready to go this weekend if Cunningham can't go again. It'll be a tough environment for Eziuka to play at Clemson, but Franklin doesn't appear to be nervous about putting him in. "He's dense; he's powerful in the weight room, and he's super trustworthy," Franklin said at his Wednesday media availability . "Obviously, everybody uses that quote: 'Do your job.' He's that guy. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Texas is looking to end a two-game skid and get its College Football Playoff hopes back on track against an Ole Miss team coming off its best performance of the year so far Getty Images Arch Manning grew up with Ole Miss all around him. His uncle Eli's jersey was retired in Oxford, and so was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State . He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma , and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons , who has a high ankle sprain. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has redisovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week. Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation : Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. Life without Colin Simmons : Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%). Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida : The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home : Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards. Where to watch Ole Miss vs. Texas live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV : ABC | Live stream : Fubo ( try free ) Ole Miss vs. Texas: prediction, picks Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight. Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. picks.headline: Ole Miss on SI staff predictions: No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas
picks.blurb: No. 7 Ole Miss will take on its fifth-ranked opponent of the season when it travels to Austin to meet No. 19 Texas in Week 8. The Rebels picked up a critical win against Missouri in dominant fashion, while Texas picked up its second-straight loss in Week 7. Texas is playing with its back against the wall and is in a ‘must-win’ spot. Ole Miss desperately wants to avoid the position the Longhorns are currently in, considering the Rebels’ path the rest of the way. Going into the weekend, Ole Miss’ strength of schedule is No. 12 and its strength of record is No. 9 in the country, according to ESPN’s FPI. A win on Saturday would go a long way for the Rebels’ resume and they aren't taking the struggling Longhorns lightly either. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Longhorns is set for 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC. Ole Miss enters the weekend as 3.5-point underdogs. Ahead of the Rebels' latest top-25 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Going into the year, and after the first three weeks of the season, Week 8 was a game I was fairly confident penciling in a loss for Ole Miss. However, now we’re actually here. With the new developments for each side throughout the month of October heading into this weekend, I like Ole Miss to get the job done in one of the country’s hardest atmospheres. Not to mention Texas won’t have some of its best players available, including Colin Simmons. He’s the type of player that’s a true game-wrecker and likely a top-10 pick in this spring’s NFL Draft. Considering Ole Miss is expected to start a true sophomore still gaining valuable experience at right tackle and a banged up Terez Davis at left tackle, there’s no telling how much of an impact Simmons could’ve had on the outcome of Saturday’s game. Though encouraging, Ole Miss’ performance running the ball and defending the run against Vanderbilt didn’t convince me that the Rebels were going to turn it around in those two aspects in a snap of a finger. That said, its dominant performance against Missouri did. Both games, particularly against the Tigers last week, were necessary confidence boosters for Ole Miss going into this weekend. Arch Manning appears to be pressing and Texas as a whole is in a make-or-break moment. It won’t be easy as the Rebels will certainly get the kitchen sink thrown at them by Texas, but I think Ole Miss pulls out another tight one. Ole Miss 30, Texas 24 Matt Galatzan This is pretty simple. If the Texas offense doesn't show up, Ole Miss is going to win by multiple scores. The Longhorns have an immeasurable amount of talent on that side of the ball, but the process, the protection and the quarterback have all been a disaster over the last few weeks. The Texas defense can keep them in this one, but it is all going to fall on the shoulders of Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, and the offense. Give me the better quarterback, and the better running game. Ole Miss 31, Texas 28 This is the most difficult prediction of the season so far for me. Texas has its back against the wall and really needs to win this game to keep its College Football Playoff hopes going strong. Ole Miss can afford one loss, but would not like to be in Texas’ current position on Nov. 7 when Georgia comes to Oxford. Logically, I want to pick Ole Miss because of the combination of the faith I have in the tandem of Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy, Texas having key players like Colin Simmons and likely Hollywood Smothers out with injuries. Also, Ole Miss’ defense seems to be peaking coming off a 31-3 win over Missouri. However, my gut just won’t let me pick against a desperate Texas team in a sold-out home game on a Saturday night. Give me the Longhorns to bounce back from two straight losses and beat Ole Miss in a close game. Texas 31, Ole Miss 28 Zion Trammell Ole Miss is coming off its best defensive performance of the season while Texas is struggling to find its offensive identity. The Longhorns have plenty of talent to succeed, which makes this matchup nerve-wracking. The Rebels have to grab an early lead and take the home crowd out of the game. I think Ole Miss will lean on Kewan Lacy and the Rebels will steal a huge road win. Cooper Ferguson I really do think that with the right system, Arch Manning can be a top-tier quarterback. He has the arm talent to compete with anyone in the nation, but the offensive line in front of him doesn't let him show it. Ole Miss wins through a defense that has grown increasingly strong over the past few weeks. For the first time in over a decade, Texas and Ole Miss meet on Saturday at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Longhorns are 3.5-point home favorites, and despite back-to-back losses, my Ole Miss vs. Texas prediction and college football picks project Arch Manning to pull off a win against his namesake's alma mater. TOP PICK Who will win Ole Miss vs Texas: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. It's a good time to buy low on a Texas team I would take to cover up to -5.5 at home against Ole Miss . While the Longhorns have lost two straight, they still have the clear defensive advantage, even with Colin Simmons unlikely to play. The Texas defense ranks sixth nationally in available yards percentage (31.2%) and 14th in havoc rate (20%). Meanwhile, the Ole Miss defense struggled in ranked matchups away from home, allowing 90 points across two games. It's a big ask for Trinidad Chambliss to make up for his own defense again against one of the top defenses in the country. Center Brycen Sanders was upgraded from questionable to probable on the SEC's Friday availability report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT, putting the Rebels one step closer to having their starting center back for Saturday night's game in Austin. On the other hand, left tackle Terez Davis remains questionable. The rest of the Ole Miss report is unchanged from Thursday. For Texas, the news went the other way. Running back Hollywood Smothers was downgraded from doubtful to out, and wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman were both downgraded from questionable to out. The Longhorns also added offensive lineman Jackson Christian as questionable. Edge rushers Colin Simmons and Richard Wesley remain out. Upgraded: OL Brycen Sanders, from questionable to probable. WR Kaliq Lockett and OL Jaydon Chatman, from questionable to out. Added: OL Jackson Christian, listed as questionable. No change: EDGE Colin Simmons and EDGE Richard Wesley remain out, and RB Derrek Cooper remains probable. The offensive line. Sanders moving to probable is the biggest news of the night for the Rebels. He and Davis both left last week's win over Missouri, and Ole Miss adjusted without missing a beat. Patrick Kutas slid from right guard to center, Troy Everett stepped in at guard and Connor Howes moved over to fill in for Davis. The Rebels still ran for a season-high 257 yards, and Pro Football Focus graded the line as the best in the FBS for the week. The secondary. Ole Miss will still be thin in the defensive backfield. Edwin Joseph, the starting nickel, will miss a second straight game after a tightrope procedure on his ankle, and MJ Preston and Pat Broomfield are also out. away.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). Simmons going down during the Florida game is a huge blow for the Texas defense, as he has been playing at an extremely high level. Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp is going to need all hands on deck on Saturday to defend Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has been one of the most dynamic playmakers in the country at the quarterback position, especially with the surprise news that Wesley is out. On top of that, Ole Miss will likely have star running back Kewan Lacy back on the field, as he is listed as probable on tonight’s injury report. The initial SEC injury report was released for the Saturday matchup between the No. 19 Texas Longhorns and against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Wednesday and while the Rebels have many more players on their side of the injury report, there are certainly some notable names for the Longhorns as well. Every game moving forward is a must-win for the Longhorns after dropping the last two matchups. away.headline: Steve Sarkisian sees a major challenge ahead against Ole Miss, and injuries aren’t helping
away.blurb: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian knows his defense isn't going to keep Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss bottled up for four quarters Saturday night. Even with a great defense, the Longhorns’ coach isn’t pretending otherwise. “He's going to get out of the pocket,” Sarkisian said on Thursday . “I'd love to say, hey, we're going to come out of this game for four quarters and he's not going to get out. He's going to get out.” And that's a problem for the Longhorns, one made considerably worse by the absence of two edge rushers. Texas will be without star pass rusher Colin Simmons and freshman Richard Wesley, both of whom were ruled out on Thursday's SEC availability report. Simmons' absence is particularly significant. The junior leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss through six games. He's accounted for more than half of Texas' 19 sacks and has been the centerpiece of a defense allowing just 272.5 yards per game. Wesley, a highly regarded freshman, was expected to help compensate for Simmons' absence before suffering an injury of his own during practice this week. That leaves Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp trying to contain one of college football's most elusive quarterbacks with a depleted pass rush. Chambliss has thrown for 1,676 yards and 14 touchdowns while adding six rushing scores. Ole Miss has allowed just five sacks all season, a testament to both its offensive line and Chambliss' ability to avoid pressure. But as Sarkisian explained, the danger isn't necessarily Chambliss taking off downfield. “It's not always about him scrambling to run,” Sarkisian said. “It's him scrambling to buy time to create the second play in the passing game, the explosive plays down the field.” That's what makes defending Chambliss particularly difficult. Even when the initial play breaks down, he can extend it long enough for receivers to find openings in the secondary. Sarkisian said Texas must maintain disciplined rushing lanes to limit those opportunities. And when Chambliss inevitably escapes, the secondary has to stay with its assignments rather than allowing an explosive completion. “The people that have defended him the best have tried to minimize him getting out of the pocket, but also not giving up those big kind of home run plays when the first play breaks down and it goes to the second play,” Sarkisian said. Doing that without Simmons won't be easy, though. “You never like losing good players,” Sarkisian said. “That part's disappointing, but that's also part of football, and that's why you have to recruit to the depth that I think we have to withstand some of the injuries that occur.” Ole Miss has injury concerns of its own. Starting offensive linemen Terez Davis and Brycen Sanders were listed as questionable Thursday, potentially complicating the Rebels' efforts to protect Chambliss. home.headline: FRIDAY Ole Miss vs. Texas Injury Report: Brycen Sanders Upgraded, Hollywood Smothers Out
home.blurb: FRIDAY Ole Miss vs. Texas Injury Report: Brycen Sanders Upgraded, Hollywood Smothers Out ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss got good news on its offensive line Friday night, and Texas' injury list got longer. Center Brycen Sanders was upgraded from questionable to probable on the SEC's Friday availability report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT, putting the Rebels one step closer to having their starting center back for Saturday night's game in Austin. On the other hand, left tackle Terez Davis remains questionable. The rest of the Ole Miss report is unchanged from Thursday. For Texas, the news went the other way. Running back Hollywood Smothers was downgraded from doubtful to out, and wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman were both downgraded from questionable to out. The Longhorns also added offensive lineman Jackson Christian as questionable. Edge rushers Colin Simmons and Richard Wesley remain out. Upgraded: OL Brycen Sanders, from questionable to probable. No change: OL Terez Davis remains questionable, and all eight players listed as out on Thursday remain out. Downgraded: RB Hollywood Smothers, from doubtful to out. WR Kaliq Lockett and OL Jaydon Chatman, from questionable to out. Added: OL Jackson Christian, listed as questionable. No change: EDGE Colin Simmons and EDGE Richard Wesley remain out, and RB Derrek Cooper remains probable. The offensive line. Sanders moving to probable is the biggest news of the night for the Rebels. He and Davis both left last week's win over Missouri, and Ole Miss adjusted without missing a beat. Patrick Kutas slid from right guard to center, Troy Everett stepped in at guard and Connor Howes moved over to fill in for Davis. The Rebels still ran for a season-high 257 yards, and Pro Football Focus graded the line as the best in the FBS for the week. The secondary. Ole Miss will still be thin in the defensive backfield. Edwin Joseph, the starting nickel, will miss a second straight game after a tightrope procedure on his ankle, and MJ Preston and Pat Broomfield are also out. Nick Cull filled in at nickel against Missouri with three tackles and a pass breakup. At cornerback, the Rebels list Jaylon Braxton and Jalyn Crawford as co-starters on one side and Antonio Kite and Dorian Barney on the other. The running game. With Smothers out, Texas will be without half of the running back rotation that Pete Golding called “a really good one-two punch that would start at most places in the country.” Smothers has 289 rushing yards this season. More of the load will now fall on Raleek Brown, who has 265 yards and a team-high five rushing touchdowns, with Derrek Cooper also available. The offensive line. Chatman being ruled out and Christian being added as questionable could leave the Texas line shuffling, just like Ole Miss did last week. That could make it harder for the Longhorns

home.headline: Texas releases injury report for Ole Miss matchup
home.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). Simmons going down during the Florida game is a huge blow for the Texas defense, as he has been playing at an extremely high level. Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp is going to need all hands on deck on Saturday to defend Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has been one of the most dynamic playmakers in the country at the quarterback position, especially with the surprise news that Wesley is out. On top of that, Ole Miss will likely have star running back Kewan Lacy back on the field, as he is listed as probable on tonight’s injury report. The initial SEC injury report was released for the Saturday matchup between the No. 19 Texas Longhorns and against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Wednesday and while the Rebels have many more players on their side of the injury report, there are certainly some notable names for the Longhorns as well. Every game moving forward is a must-win for the Longhorns after dropping the last two matchups. They will need to get healthy moving forward as they try to navigate a difficult stretch in the schedule with eight straight games to close the season.

home.blurb: Texas football has not played well over the past two weeks, and there’s a good chance that Arch Manning will be benched as KJ Lacey Jr. is expected to take some first-team reps this week. LeBron's biggest comeback Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs Vanderbilt: Final Thoughts & Prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Fri, October 23, 2026 at 8:49 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football hosts Vanderbilt tomorrow night under the lights of Kroger Field as the Wildcats look to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. We previewed Vanderbilt's offense and defense as they are in a massive transition year. We also list our X factors for the game on both sides of the football. After laying out Kentucky 's path to victory in this game, I will now give my final thoughts and prediction. Kentucky is playing a night game in front of a sold out Kroger Field, and this will be true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis' first road SEC night game. The city is buzzing watching year one of Will Stein and the big blue nation will certainly play a factor in this football game. Kentucky's coaching staff is ensuring this team does not overlook the Commodores, as they are reminding them the beatdown they suffered last season in Nashville and the incident of Vanderbilt players disrespecting the UK logo at midfield last time they were in Lexington. There are plenty of impact players for the Wildcats that remember the whooping they took last season, so I do not think Kentucky will sleep walk their way into the bye week. As we stated when we laid out Kentucky's path to victory, this game is a massive advantage for the Wildcats on the line of scrimmage. Kentucky's offensive line has been incredible this season, and I expect them to get a ton of movement in the running game as well as keeping quarterback Kenny Minchey clean in the pocket. On the other side of the football, Kentucky's defensive line should dominate this Vanderbilt offensive line. Jared Curtis will be facing pressure, but the key for the Wildcats is to get him on the ground and not let him extend plays by erasing sack opportunities. Another key area is always the turnover margin, and Kentucky is one of the best teams in the nation at winning the turnover margin consistently. Statistically, Kentucky ranks third in FBS with a +11 turnover margin, trailing only New Mexico and Notre Dame. This is a large advantage in Kentucky's favor, as Curtis is a true freshman and already has multiple interceptions and fumbles on the season. If Kentucky can continue to win the turnover battle as they have all season, this game has blowout potential. Kentucky's offense has yet to put it all together, we saw them at their best on the road at Texas A&M in a dominant third quarter performance. This could be the game where it clicks for four quarters for this offense. Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in success rate and explosive play rate combined. Vanderbilt is dead last in the conference in success rate allowed and they rank bottom five in the SEC in explosive play rate allowed. This is a huge opportunity for the Wildcats to put on an offensive showcase against an SEC team to go into the bye week on a high note. This game is monumental for Kentucky, and we have seen SEC teams struggle the game before their bye week this season. Kentucky has to put together a great game to go into a bye week where they could be a top ten team in the country the next time they take the field if they can get this win. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen over that bye week and if the Wildcats take care of business, they will be on the graphic. A win here could set up a November to remember for the Wildcats where everything is on the table from SEC Championship to College Football Playoff talks. Prediction: Kentucky 42, Vanderbilt 17 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Vanderbilt: Final Thoughts & Prediction

LeBron's biggest comeback Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week. LeBron's biggest comeback Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. away.headline: Kentucky gets major injury boost ahead of Vanderbilt game
away.blurb: Thankfully, Kentucky just received some huge news on star running back CJ Baxter. According to On3’s Pete Nakos, Baxter has officially been removed from the SEC’s injury report and is on track to play Saturday against Vanderbilt. Baxter missed last week’s win over Oklahoma while dealing with a hamstring injury. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, meanwhile, has been ruled out for the game. Kentucky has been one of the biggest surprises in college football this season. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have surged to a 6-1 record, climbed to No. 12 in the AP Top 25, and put themselves firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Their only loss came against Alabama in Week 2, but they’ve now rattled off five straight wins. Kentucky has already picked up impressive wins over Texas A&M, South Carolina, LSU, and Oklahoma, but Saturday brings another test: SEC rival Vanderbilt. The Commodores have struggled this season, dropping four straight to sit 3-4 on the season, but the Wildcats can’t afford to get too comfortable with how many upsets we’ve seen in recent weeks. More news : Michigan State Gets Concerning QB Injury News Ahead of UCLA Game Baxter, a senior transfer from Texas, is Kentucky’s leading running back, having already produced 484 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns on 87 carries, averaging 5.6 yards per carry, along with 62 receiving yards on seven catches. His best game came against South Alabama when he rushed for 149 yards and one touchdown on just 16 carries (9.3 yards per carry). He later ran for 123 yards and two touchdowns against LSU. Without him against Oklahoma, Kentucky ran for just 72 total rushing yards and put up just 21 points in the win, their second-lowest scoring total of the season. Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes helped fill the void, but Baxter is the more proven lead back who can wear down defenses, pick up tough yards, and take pressure off quarterback Kenny Minchey. More news : Notre Dame Told to Look in the Mirror After BYU Loss More news : Lane Kiffin Gets Good News on 2 LSU Stars Before Auburn Game Kentucky has put itself in a good position to make the CFP, but there’s still more work to do. Saturday’s game against Vanderbilt is important for the Wildcats to protect their winning streak and build momentum with a tough stretch of games ahead. After the Commodores, Kentucky will head to No. 11 Tennessee, host No. 20 Florida and travel to No. 22 Missouri before their season closer against rival Louisville. away.headline: Initial Vanderbilt Football Injury Report Before Trip to No. 12 Kentucky
away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. Vanderbilt’s initial injury report. Davin Chandler and Dontae Carter both questionable, Cayden Daniels probable and Josiah Broxton doubtful. pic.twitter.com/aDGBMzaMl8 Initial Vanderbilt Football Injury Report Before Trip to No. 12 Kentucky Skip to main content SI.COM More from Vanderbilt Commodores FOOTBALL The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. Follow us on Twitter/X , Facebook , YouTube , Instagram , and TikTok for the latest news. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 16 USC, which has rebounded from the Oregon loss with back-to-back wins, seeks to improve its road record to 3-0 on Saturday night in Wisconsin Getty Images When you look around the Big Ten these days, there's a lot of uncertainty. Nearly half the league is down to its backup quarterback, whether due to injury or by choice. The only undefeated team in the conference is UCLA , while Oregon's conference title hopes are hanging on by a thread. Ohio State just picked up a huge win, but faces the prospect of being without Julian Sayin for the rest of the season. It's chaos, and when chaos is around, there's a chance someone unexpected will emerge and take advantage of it. So while No. 16 USC's trip to Madison this weekend to face Wisconsin might not be the headliner game of the weekend, it's a chance for two teams to step forward and stake a claim in the conference. USC has won two straight since dropping a game to Oregon, and perhaps most surprisingly, one of those wins has come on the road. The Trojans are 2-0 outside the Coliseum, which has been a serious problem for them during Lincoln Riley's tenure. Now they're back on the road facing a Wisconsin team coming off its first Big Ten loss at UCLA last week. The winner stays in the Big Ten title race with a chance to capitalize on the chaos. The loser will have to hope for a lot more chaos to befall the rest of the league going forward. USC vs. Wisconsin: Need to know Wisconsin has struggled with USC: They haven't shared a conference for long, but there is familiarity with these programs. Familiarity Wisconsin would sooner forget. USC is 7-1 all time against the Badgers, with the lone loss coming in the 2015 Holiday Bowl. They've only played once as Big Ten foes, and USC won that game 38-21 in Los Angeles during the 2024 season. As for the trip to Camp Randall, USC has won both the games in Madison, though the last meeting came in 1965. NCAA eligibility rules change every day, but I'm pretty sure none of the players who played in that game have remaining eligibility. Lincoln Riley is good off a bye: While Wisconsin was in Los Angeles losing to UCLA last week, USC was in Los Angeles chilling on the couch watching. That's typically been a good thing for the Trojans. Under Lincoln Riley, USC is 5-1 coming off a bye and has won three straight. Wisconsin has performed poorly in these spots of late: Wisconsin has played six home games against AP-ranked opponents under Luke Fickell. It has won only once in those six games. That win came last season against No. 24 Washington . As for the five losses, four of them have come by at least 14 points, though all four of them were against top-4 teams in the poll. Where to watch USC vs. Wisconsin live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Camp Randall Stadium -- Madison, Wisconsin TV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) USC vs. Wisconsin prediction, picks Wisconsin is probably looking at the weather forecast for this game and wondering what it did to offend the weather gods. If there was any time to wish for temperatures in the 40s with biting wind, it's when USC is coming to town. Instead, the forecast is calling for temperatures in the 60s with a manageable breeze. Still, even if the weather won't have an oversized impact, I like the under here. USC may have won its two road trips so far this season, but the offense didn't look great against Penn State , and this Wisconsin defense is good. I also don't have much faith in the Wisconsin offense. Two weeks after preparing for the "White Out" at Penn State, USC turned the volume up on campus over the practice speakers again. But this time to prepare for another historically loud environment: The home of the Wisconsin Badgers. This is another road venue that coach Lincoln Riley isn't familiar with. Or even past Big Ten defender at Michigan State Alex VanSumeren . So Madison becomes a whole new environment for these Trojans, leading into this deeper dive for the Oct. 24 showdown. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Saturday night in Camp Randall Stadium could easily set the tone for the rest of the year for Wisconsin football. A win would instantly erase the pain from Week 7 out in Los Angeles, as it would represent Wisconsin's first victory over a legitimately good opponent and give head coach Luke Fickell another top-20 upset on his resume for the 2026 season, which would go a long way in helping him prove he's the man for the job in Madison. A loss, on the other hand, would even up the Badgers' Big Ten record at 2-2 and set them up with a must-win on Halloween in Iowa City, a situation nobody wants to be in. As Wisconsin continues prep for the Trojans , here's three bold predictions for the Saturday night showdown: Wisconsin shuts down star Trojans' tailback King Miller USC Trojans running back King Miller. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. Instead, Wisconsin held the Bruins to 44 rushing yards through the first three quarters (120 after a fourth quarter of mostly clock control from UCLA) while Knight himself posted just 23 yards on 13 carries. All told, UCLA averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. Surprisingly, that didn't matter because the Badgers couldn't contain Bruins' quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who completed 67% of his passes while tossing for 264 yards. But Wisconsin made a point; even the best rushing attacks in college football should expect to struggle against the Cardinal and White. USC has two very capable backs in King Miller (114 carries, 595 yards, four touchdowns) and Waymond Jordan (63 carries, 287 yards and two scores). However, the Trojans' ground game as a whole ranks just 77th nationally, one spot above the Badgers — both teams run for 152 yards per game. While USC's backs are capable, this isn't the most impressive rushing attack and Wisconsin just proved that it can make even the best ground games in the country struggle mightily. Miller has yet to run for fewer than 45 yards this season; I foresee that happening Saturday night. Colton Joseph takes care of the ball all night Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. Against USC, there's no reason why he can't make it three. The Trojans have only intercepted three passes this fall across seven games; there's only 11 FBS programs that've played as many games and picked off fewer passes. Their pass defense as a whole has left plenty to be desired; USC is allowing 239 passing yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Joseph has also cut down on the "turnover-worthy plays," according to Pro Football Focus. After he combined for eight over the Badgers' first four games, he has just one over the last two games. The turnover battle is going to be huge in order to pull off an upset like this, but I think Joseph can keep it clean Saturday night. Wisconsin benches PJ Wilkins Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. At what point does Wisconsin give up on Wilkins as a starting-caliber offensive lineman this season? It's tried him at three spots — left tackle, right tackle and right guard — all of which have been problematic. He easily "leads" the team with 12 pressures, per Pro Football Focus, although having watched the all-22 tape I'd venture to say that's a generously low estimate. He just doesn't appear to have the quickness to hold up in pass protection. “It’s been a little bit difficult. When guys get dinged up, in particular Kawecki and moving Stylz back in there, we just felt like that was our best five," Fickell said this week . "We gotta find a way to make sure we have our best five up front every week.” Unfortunately, it's pretty clear the Badgers' "best five" doesn't include Wilkins at this point in time. With Kawecki probable as of the Wednesday injury report, he could return to center, meaning Blackmon could return to right guard. For the third time in just over a month, USC travels east for a Big Ten road game on Saturday, Oct. 24, this time for prime-time action against Wisconsin at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisc., at 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC). The Trojans are 2.5-point road favorites, and my USC vs. Wisconsin prediction and college football picks expect Lincoln Riley's program to stay undefeated on the road. TOP PICK Who will win USC vs Wisconsin: USC -2.5 USC has long faced criticism for its performances in cross-country road games under Lincoln Riley, but the Trojans beat Penn State by eight points in Week 6 at Happy Valley, covering as 1.5-point favorites. Fresh off a bye week, I like USC to cover -2.5 or better on the road against Wisconsin . The Badgers and Trojans are so different it's like they're playing completely different sports, and that favors USC. Wisconsin lost by double digits on the West Coast last week to a UCLA team led by a backup QB making his first start as a Bruin, and Jayden Maiava is a lot scarier than Ty Dieffenbach. Maiava ranks in the Top 10 nationally in QBR (86.8) and is protected by one of the best offensive lines in the country, with the starting five credited with allowing just two sacks . If Wisconsin can't pressure Maiava, he'll pick the Badgers apart, and the Badgers won't be able to throw themselves back into the game. USC is also expected to have its most disruptive defensive player back, with Jahkeem Stewart listed as probable on the Big Ten injury report . USC vs Wisconsin Over/Under pick: Over 49.5 This is the lowest game total of the season for USC, and that's because Wisconsin is the polar opposite type of team. But even with the Badgers' strong defense and lackluster offense, I would take the Over at 50.5 or better. In four Big Ten matchups, USC has averaged 31.2 points per game while allowing 26.5, with the game total reaching 54 or higher three times . The dual-threat ability of Badgers QB Colton Joseph should allow him to make enough of a dent against a Trojans defense ranked outside the Top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and early-down EPA per play. USC has only held one opponent below 21 points this season, and has only had one opponent hold it below 27. USC vs Wisconsin combo USC's defense remains a huge concern, but with one of the best QBs in college football, an elite offensive line, and a half-dozen quality playmakers, the Trojans have enough firepower to win another game in Big Ten country. Maiava has too much firepower to utilize for Wisconsin's defense to hold for four quarters, and this is the best offense the Badgers have faced. USC ranks No. 2 nationally in net adjusted EPA per play on offense . If Stewart and USC's talented defensive line come to play against a Wisconsin front that struggles to run the ball — the Badgers rank 115th in rushing success rate (39.2%) — the Trojans can pull away late. It doesn't have a signature win, and it lost at home to Oregon, but it beat Penn State and Washington. Realistically, the Trojans will go to the College Football Playoff if they close 5-1. However, with what's coming next, they can't afford to miss in Madison. Wisconsin is still alive for big things, too. And here's the funky part – the rest of the schedule isn't that bad. Beat USC, and all of a sudden, the team whose only losses are to Notre Dame and UCLA will be in the thick of the hunt. USC vs Wisconsin: Quick Hits USC gets Ohio State and goes to Indiana after this, and then after facing Maryland, it closes in the Rose Bowl against UCLA. Wisconsin goes on the road for three of its next four games, starting with Iowa before hosting Rutgers. USC is 7-1 all-time in the series, highlighted by a classic 42-37 win in the 1963 Rose Bowl. Passing accuracy. Wisconsin's passing game isn't sharp enough. Dante Moore and Dylan Raiola combined to connect on 77% of their passes in Oregon's win over USC. Louisiana's Lunch Winfield gave the Trojans fits in the 49-30 Ragin' Cajun loss, and Penn State kept it close two weeks ago with Rocco Becht hitting 66% of his throws. Badger quarterback Colton Joseph is a good all-around quarterback, but over the last two games he has only completed 15 of his last 36 throws. For all the improvements, the Badgers are still 133rd in the nation in first downs, and they have to somehow control the offensive narrative. Why Wisconsin Will Win The Badger defense has been terrific. It might have been a loss, but the run defense was the only one to keep UCLA's ground game under wraps. The secondary held both Penn State and Michigan State to under a 48% completion rate. USC might have a devastating midrange passing game when Jayden Maiava gets going, but things have slowed down a bit. The one loss to Oregon came when he completed just 55% of his throws. Wisconsin is allowing teams to complete 57% of their passes. USC vs Wisconsin Prediction, Betting Lines Can Colton Joseph get hot? The conditions in Madison will be perfect, and the Wisconsin defense will keep this close, but Joseph has to be accurate, and he needs to be excellent on the move. Wisconsin doesn't have a pass rush to get to Maiava, and it doesn't take the ball away. Joseph and the Badgers will come close, but they won't be able to close out enough drives with touchdowns to pull this off.
