LeBron's biggest comeback Behind enemy lines: USC expert previews Week 8 matchup at Wisconsin Jordon Lawrenz, Badgers Wire Fri, October 23, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Wisconsin Badgers return to Madison on Saturday, Oct. 24, for a primetime showdown against No. 15 USC . USC is fresh off a bye week, while Wisconsin made the West Coast trip to UCLA, where they fell at the Rose Bowl, 17-7 . It was an embarrassing offensive performance for Luke Fickell's squad, yet somehow they hung in there against a team that has now cracked the top 10 in the US LBM Coaches Poll . With Week 7 rapidly approaching, Badgers Wire's Jordon Lawrenz had a chance to speak with Trojans Wire 's Matt Zemek ahead of the Big Ten matchup. Fresh off a bye week, do you think USC will be able to carry its momentum from the Washington and Penn State wins in Madison? The lesson of the Lincoln Riley era at USC is not to expect the Trojans to do anything the easy way. They did win at Penn State, which marks real improvement for a program that has consistently struggled to win Big Ten road games under Riley. However, that's a low bar. We can all see how mediocre Penn State is. The Nittany Lions lost to Michigan after losing to USC. The Trojans have a below-average defense, and so USC might be the get-right tonic for Wisconsin's offense. Should USC be favored? Probably, based on its eight-point win at Penn State. Does this mean the Trojans will get the job done? Hardly. This feels like a very close game, but whether USC wins or loses, don't expect the Trojans to have a smooth evening with no bumps in the road. It's not how they have historically operated on the road under Lincoln Riley. Who do you think the bye week benefited the most? Are there are any players who were banged up or are dealing with injuries? USC did need a week off. Not only does an off week give players a chance to rest, but in USC's case, the Trojans had played on seven consecutive weekends dating all the way back to August 29. When a team plays on that many consecutive weekends, it really needs a break. The key player USC is likely to get back for the Wisconsin game is tight end Mark Bowman. He has potential as a downfield pass catcher, but he is already a very good blocker who adds structure and balance to the USC offense. The Trojans were missing something when he was out the past few weeks. Trent Mosley is a more important player, but Bowman is right behind him in terms of value to USC's offense and quarterback Jayden Maiava. There are some defensive players who have a chance to get healthy during the off week, but the defense is a lot weaker than the offense. It's more important for the offense to be able to max out. That's where the off week can help USC more. What grade would you give Jayden Maiava through his first seven games this season? Jayden Maiava gets a B+. This might be a harsh grade, given that Maiava can't be blamed too much for the problems of the defense, but it remains that USC did not score 30 points against either Oregon or Washington. Maiava was solid against Oregon, but erratic against Washington. He has generally been very, very good. He played well at Penn State. However, for me to give an A to a USC quarterback requires that he rises to the moment in all the big games and all the defining situations a quarterback faces. He didn't do that against Oregon, so I have to limit him to a B+. I am holding him to a very high standard, because I think he's better than Dante Moore of Oregon and Arch Manning of Texas, among others. If he wants the highest possible grade, he will need to beat Ohio State or Indiana for sure. With Ohio State, Indiana, and UCLA on the schedule down the stretch, just how important is it to leave Camp Randall with a win? This is a must-win for Lincoln Riley with the brutal schedule ahead. USC will have a tough time beating Ohio State, Indiana, and UCLA. The Trojans have to finish 10-2 to make the playoff and convince everyone they are back where they belong in the college football world. Until they do that, they are an unproven team and a failed program. Beating Wisconsin is absolutely necessary to save Lincoln Riley's job. A loss here means USC could easily finish 8-4, which is nowhere near good enough for the program, the administration, and most of all, the fans. A loss here would have the pitchforks out for Riley. He would go into the Ohio State-Indiana gauntlet in huge trouble, and the roof could cave in on him. A loss to Wisconsin is an absolute and unmitigated disaster for the Trojans. In what areas do you believe USC has the edge over Wisconsin in this game? USC's main advantage is at quarterback. Maiava versus Colton Joseph is a mismatch. UCLA absolutely smothered Joseph and the rest of the Wisconsin offense. Maiava plays for Lincoln Riley, one of the best quarterback coaches in modern times, and has been above average on a consistent basis this season, the Washington game being the one primary exception. This is where USC has to create separation from Wisconsin. Maiava playing up to his standard, or even close to it, will give USC the clear upper hand. Wisconsin will need Maiava to have an off night in order to pull off the upset. Final score prediction? USC 27, Wisconsin 20. USC doesn't blow out Big Ten opponents on the road at night, but Wisconsin just isn't in a position to score enough to overcome a much more talented USC team. away.blurb: The week off allowed some key starters to get healthy, while a couple of others will still be a game-time decision. What is the latest injury report for the Trojans heading into this Big Ten showdown? Left tackle Elijah Paige, a Midseason first team All-American by The Athletic, was a late add to injury report against Penn State on Oct. 10 and was ultimately held out. USC turned to true freshman Vlad Dyakonov, who made his first career start, and he excelled. But having Paige back in the lineup is a massive boost for the offensive line. The Trojans will also get back left guard Hayden Treter, who has been out since going down in the first half against Oregon on Sept. 26. Kaylon Miller has started in his place. Tight end Mark Bowman has missed each of the last two games and is questionable heading into Saturday's game against the Badgers. Having Bowman back in the lineup would impact the run and pass game. Receivers Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are out for the season, but USC did get back freshman receiver Trent Mosley returned to the lineup against Penn State, after missing the previous three games. He was a true game-time decision but immediately looked like the player that caught the attention of the college football world. Freshman receiver Luc Weaver saw his first significant action against Penn State because of the numerous injuries in front of him. He is listed as questionable this week. Defensive lineman Jahkeem Stewart is still on the injury report but is listed as probable. Stewart missed the first four games of the season after dealing with the same foot injury that hampered him last season. Defensive lineman Jide Abasiri is questionable. The junior played just one snap against Penn State after suffering a lower body injury on the final drive against Washington on Oct. 3. Abasiri is second on the team in tackles for loss. If Abasiri is unable to go, freshmen Jaimeon Winfield and Tomuhini Topui will continue to see an increased role. Linebacker Jadyn Walker is probable for Saturday's contest. Walker has been a key reserve this season behind Desman Stephens and Deven Bryant. Ta'Mere Robinson and Elijah Newby have also been key reserves this season. home.blurb: Whether he just wasn’t quite ready or the Wisconsin staff wanted to play it safe, he stayed out against the Bruins, with more than half a season left. Stylz Blackmon, who had been playing right guard, moved to center to replace Kawecki, while PJ Wilkins slotted into guard. Now, Kawecki has been upgraded to ‘Probable’ ahead of the Badgers’ matchup with the Trojans. Kawecki’s return would be a nice boost for the offensive line that struggled mightily against UCLA last week. A pair of starters are ‘questionable’ for Saturday Two starters popped up on the report this week that we didn’t expect. Wide receiver Malachi Coleman and cornerback Javan Robinson are both listed as ‘questionable’ for Saturday. RB Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ The Badgers got Abu Sama back off the injury report last week, but injuries remain at the position. After missing last week’s game against UCLA, Nate Palmer remains ‘doubtful’ for this week’s game. Palmer has received only a handful of carries this season, but he has been a constant presence on special teams and the team’s primary kick returner, returning six kicks for an average of 28.2 yards per return. Christian Borman Oct 22, 2026 Share Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Malachi Coleman. Some players are trending in the right direction after missing time, but a couple of names on the report weren’t expected. Here’s where things stand three days ahead of the matchup with the Trojans. Austin Kawecki is trending in the right direction Starting center Austin Kawecki left in the middle of the Badgers’ game with Michigan State in Week 5. With a bye week to rest, there was hope he would be back for the Badgers’ road game against UCLA in Week 7. Javan Robinson has been the most consistent cornerback for the Badgers this season. If he misses the game, it would be a massive blow to the defense, especially in a week when they face one of the best passing quarterbacks in the country, Jordan Maiava. On top of that, the cornerback depth has already taken a hit this year after Cai Bates was lost for the season with a knee injury early in the year. Losing Coleman wouldn’t be ideal, either. But the passing attack for the Badgers has been inconsistent, and even after his breakout game against Notre Dame in Week 1, he hasn’t been the force we all hoped he’d be. Fortunately for the Badgers, they just got Jaylon Domingeaux back from injury last week and caught a pair of passes, so there is at least some more depth at receiver. home.headline: USC Trojans Injury Questions vs. Wisconsin Badgers
home.blurb: The week off allowed some key starters to get healthy, while a couple of others will still be a game-time decision. What is the latest injury report for the Trojans heading into this Big Ten showdown? Left tackle Elijah Paige, a Midseason first team All-American by The Athletic, was a late add to injury report against Penn State on Oct. 10 and was ultimately held out. USC turned to true freshman Vlad Dyakonov, who made his first career start, and he excelled. But having Paige back in the lineup is a massive boost for the offensive line. The Trojans will also get back left guard Hayden Treter, who has been out since going down in the first half against Oregon on Sept. 26. Kaylon Miller has started in his place. Tight end Mark Bowman has missed each of the last two games and is questionable heading into Saturday's game against the Badgers. Having Bowman back in the lineup would impact the run and pass game. Receivers Corey Simms and Terrell Anderson are out for the season, but USC did get back freshman receiver Trent Mosley returned to the lineup against Penn State, after missing the previous three games. He was a true game-time decision but immediately looked like the player that caught the attention of the college football world. Freshman receiver Luc Weaver saw his first significant action against Penn State because of the numerous injuries in front of him. He is listed as questionable this week. Defensive lineman Jahkeem Stewart is still on the injury report but is listed as probable. Stewart missed the first four games of the season after dealing with the same foot injury that hampered him last season. Defensive lineman Jide Abasiri is questionable. The junior played just one snap against Penn State after suffering a lower body injury on the final drive against Washington on Oct. 3. Abasiri is second on the team in tackles for loss. If Abasiri is unable to go, freshmen Jaimeon Winfield and Tomuhini Topui will continue to see an increased role. Linebacker Jadyn Walker is probable for Saturday's contest. Walker has been a key reserve this season behind Desman Stephens and Deven Bryant. Ta'Mere Robinson and Elijah Newby have also been key reserves this season. home.blurb: 2 Key Badgers Remain Questionable Ahead of Saturday Night vs. No. 16 USC - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF 2 Key Badgers Remain Questionable Ahead of Saturday Night vs. No. 16 USC Wisconsin could be about to receive some big-time reinforcements with starting center Austin Kawecki, who's listed on the updated Big Ten injury report as probable for the second straight day. However, two key players remain questionable ahead of the enormous showdown with No. 16 USC . Star cornerback Javan Robinson, who's been lights out for the Badgers in coverage this fall, remains questionable along with wideout Malachi Coleman, who's arguably Wisconsin's most explosive and dangerous receiver. Two running backs are also included on the report for Wisconsin. Nate Palmer, who has just nine carries for 26 yards this season, is listed as questionable. That's not the biggest cause for concern, as when starter Abu Sama has been healthy, he's the Badgers' RB4 behind Sama, Darrion Dupree and Bryan Jackson. But speaking of Dupree, he also popped up on the injury report, albeit in the "probable" category. If Robinson is unavailable, that could spell trouble for a Wisconsin secondary that looked surprisingly permeable against UCLA backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach. As I've written previously , this isn't the right week to have concerns in you rsecondary or about your pass coverage; Trojans' quarterback Jayden Maiava is No. 2 nationally in passing yards with 2,045. As for Coleman, his absence would hurt Wisconsin as well. His speed and ability to stretch defenses vertically can create all kinds of problems if he's utilized correctly. No other Wisconsin wideout has shown the ability to consistently beat defensive backs downfield. If he's indeed unavailable, expect Jaylon Domingeaux, who made his Badgers' debut in Pasadena, to take on a bigger role. North Dakota State visits New Mexico in Week 8 for a late-night Mountain West Conference showdown at University Stadium in Albuquerque. Kickoff is scheduled for 10 p.m. ET on The CW. The Bison are 4.5-point underdogs, but my North Dakota State vs. New Mexico prediction backs them to keep things competitive and potentially pull off an upset in adverse weather conditions. Here's how I'm approaching the spread, total, and combo, along with more college football picks for Saturday. TOP PICK Who will win North Dakota State vs New Mexico: North Dakota State +4.5 Playable up to 53%. North Dakota State has outgained its opponents in six of its first seven games this season , including each of its last four contests. The Bison's only outright loss in 2026 came on the road against UNLV, a game in which they finished with three more first downs and 45 more total yards than the Rebels. North Dakota State was the better team for much of that matchup but threw three interceptions, missed a field goal, and turned the ball over on downs twice. UNLV scored 10 of its 13 points off turnovers and didn't have a single offensive drive that gained more than 50 yards. New Mexico remains undefeated in conference play, but the Lobos face a difficult scheduling spot after playing in Hawaii in Week 7 . North Dakota State is a talented team with a significant travel advantage in this matchup, despite being the road underdog. North Dakota State vs New Mexico Over/Under pick: Under 40.5 Playable up to 52%. Pro Football Focus grades North Dakota State as the 22nd-best defense in the nation , and the numbers back up that ranking. The Bison have allowed 17 points or fewer in six of their seven games this season. New Mexico's defense has earned even higher marks from Pro Football Focus, ranking 19th nationally. The Lobos have held opponents to 10 points or fewer in five of their six games this fall. They also held No. 24 Oklahoma to just 14 first downs and 299 yards of total offense in a road matchup back in September. Both defenses could get some additional help from the weather on Saturday night. Rain and wind figure to make downfield passing difficult, potentially forcing both offenses to become more one-dimensional. With two highly rated defenses and challenging conditions, I'm expecting a low-scoring slugfest in this Mountain West showdown. North Dakota State vs New Mexico combo Playable up to 22%. The Lobos have since been on a tear, taking out New Mexico State, UTEP and Hawaii over the last three games on the way to a 5-1 overall run. away.headline: Former USC TE could make season debut for Lobos against North Dakota State
away.blurb: New Mexico tight end Joey Olsen is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against North Dakota State, per an availability report released by the Mountain West on Thursday. The 6-foot-5, 246-pound junior transferred to UNM in January after playing sparingly over two seasons at Southern California. He tore his ACL during offseason workouts and has been listed as out on every availability report but Thursday's. Head coach Jason Eck first indicated that Olsen could potentially return this season in August, lauding the Lake Oswego, Oregon native's work ethic in rehabbing his injury. "Joey, he's going to keep stepping up … I do think he's probably looking (to return) more near the end of this month," Eck said on Oct. 5. "Maybe that Halloween game (against San Jose State) or something would be maybe his first thing, just getting enough months (removed) from his surgery that way." If Olsen is able to return, he would provide UNM with another receiving option in a tight end room that's been led by Cade Keith (15 catches for 212 yards, 2 touchdowns). Rated as a three-star prospect out of Lakeridge (Ore.) High School, Olsen caught 36 passes for 650 yards and 11 touchdowns as a senior to finish as the Pacers' all-time receptions (119) and yards (2,303) leader. Offensive lineman Cole Millward is also listed as questionable for Saturday's game. Eck said the 6-5, 297-pound senior tweaked his ankle early in UNM's 21-10 win over Hawaii. home.blurb: After initially exhausting his eligibility, Laubstein was able to return to UNM for a sixth and final year via an NCAA waiver. A former junior college athlete, he successfully contended that at least one of his seasons spent at that level shouldn’t count toward his NCAA eligibility. James Laubstein, middle, provided a "lot of juice" for UNM, coach Jason Eck said. Mike Sandoval/Journal “Him being one of the oldest guys in the room, he taught me a lot,” Fa’avae said Tuesday. “(Laubstein) showed me the ropes and what to do, what not to do, how I should approach this, how I should approach that as a young quarterback. He taught me a lot of stuff I know today and always had my back, always helped me out. … It’s sad that got his season (taken) from him.” “We’ll have to have some element of (the) quarterback run involved,” he added. “But we gotta be careful because now two of our top four quarterbacks (Laubstein and Layne) coming into the year are out. So you don’t wanna get to less than that, you know?” Eck indicated receiver Shawn Miller (concussion) is not likely to play this week: “He’s just not coming along. He’s still battling symptoms and stuff, so he has not cleared the protocol (to return). And the longer it goes on, I think the more concerning it is because I think when you (show symptoms over an extended period of time), that kind of shows that it’s really affecting you.
